Permit FIVE wrong answers globally, using the API remaining_checks counter. (card: Holder confirmation may be asked twice. Explain the purpose of security once after a refusal; a second refusal closes br-unverified/br-r-declined. Merely asking why we need security is not refusal. Exhausted wrong answers close br-unverified/br-r-failed after "Please contact our account desk.")

Restore next-business-day-only callbacks, 09:10–16:50 inclusive, strictly after now. One opportunity to correct an invalid slot remains in force. (card: invalid or absent after that gives br-unreached/br-r-no-callback. A successfully scheduled slot gives br-unreached/br-r-callback.)

third_party.deceased_sentence: We are sorry for your loss.

source.text: If the number is wrong, use br-unreached/br-r-wrong-number; if the holder died, say "We are sorry for your loss." and use br-unreached/br-r-deceased.
Open Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday; Friday and Saturday are closed. Holidays: 2026-10-18, 2026-10-29, 2026-11-01, 2026-11-26.

Days late 1–14: replace both earlier deadlines with today plus ELEVEN calendar days, adjusted FOLLOWING to a business day. The two offer slots are unchanged. (card: Full by last business day this week, using next week if today is that day; then floor by deadline)
| 15–80 | Last business day of the current month; business basis, preceding adjustment | Full by deadline, using floor if full already refused |

Always start with the full overdue sum. Never ask how much the customer can pay. Offer the product's floor once if full is unaffordable; say "The unpaid remainder stays overdue." Accept any customer-proposed amount between floor and full inclusive

Today is allowed when it is a business day. Roll a customer-proposed non-business day forward, then cap at that product's deadline by offering the deadline for agreement. ... For a vague date ask once, then offer the deadline.

special_cases.name: already_paid
special_cases.trigger: The customer says the current overdue sum has already been paid.
special_cases.say: Payments may take three business days to reach our account view.

source.text: Current overdue sum already paid: say "Payments may take three business days to reach our account view."; mark that product br-r-settled and continue. Do not ask for a promise on that product.

special_cases.name: dispute
special_cases.trigger: The customer disputes ownership of the account or the debt, including saying a historical account was paid off while denying the current debt.

source.text: Ownership/debt dispute: mark that product br-r-disputed and continue. Historical account payoff combined with denial of current debt is a dispute, not a current-payment report.

special_cases.name: hardship
special_cases.trigger: The customer describes hardship such as job loss, illness or inability to meet essential living costs (wins over a simultaneous request for smaller instalments).
special_cases.say: I am sorry you are facing this difficulty.

source.text: Hardship includes job loss, illness and inability to meet essential living costs. Say "I am sorry you are facing this difficulty." Offer br-care-desk; if accepted transfer and close br-routed/br-r-care. ... If the care offer is declined, mark only the affected product br-r-distress and continue without persuasion. A volunteered amount/date may still be accepted after the care offer

special_cases.name: restructuring
special_cases.trigger: The customer asks to change the contract, instalments or repayment plan without hardship.

source.text: Requests to change the contract, instalments or repayment plan without hardship: transfer to br-plan-desk and close br-routed/br-r-replan; no persuasion and no promise.

special_cases.name: human
special_cases.trigger: The customer asks to speak with a human / a person.

source.text: Human request: restore ASK ONCE whether our assistant can help, then transfer only if the customer still wants a person. (card: if the customer agrees continue, otherwise transfer to br-human-desk and close br-routed/br-r-person)

special_cases.name: scam
special_cases.trigger: The customer worries the call is a scam or asks how to know the call is genuine.
special_cases.say: You may verify this call using the contact number printed on your statement.

source.text: ## Exceptions (before any collection persuasion) ... Scam concern: say the scam_reply below, then continue at the interrupted stage; not a transfer or a close.

special_cases.name: refuse_to_talk
special_cases.trigger: The customer refuses to talk or continue the conversation.

source.text: ## Exceptions (before any collection persuasion) ... Refusal to talk: ask once whether we may continue. If still refused, mark remaining unresolved products br-r-refused, stop further discussion and finalize by the outcome precedence above (do not overwrite saved promises or existing paid/dispute markers). No promise is taken after that refusal.

special_cases.name: robot
special_cases.trigger: The customer asks whether they are talking to a robot or an automated system.
special_cases.say: I am the automated assistant of Bracken Exchange Bank.

source.text: | robot_reply | I am the automated assistant of Bracken Exchange Bank. |

special_cases.name: change_saved_promise
special_cases.trigger: The customer wants to change an arrangement that was already saved.
special_cases.say: Contact our account desk to change a saved arrangement.

source.text: Changes to saved promises are directed to the stated change channel, never implemented as another write. | recorded_promise_change_reply | Contact our account desk to change a saved arrangement. |

table.when: Transfer: plan desk br-r-replan, human desk br-r-person, care desk br-r-care.
No arrangement; reason of the first non-paid product in returned order.

source.text: Promises: br-promised; all paid: br-settled; transfer: br-routed; no arrangement: br-unarranged. (card: A transfer overrides the closing result even if a promise was already recorded ... otherwise use br-unarranged with the first non-paid product's reason in returned product order ... A permanent write failure uses br-r-service ...; plain refusal uses br-r-refused. Say goodbye before close_call.)

Note endpoint vocabulary: br-r-refused, br-r-distress, br-r-disputed, br-r-settled, br-r-service. Enable notes: one note per unpromised product, deferred until the final non-transfer choice. ... No note on a successfully promised product and none on transfers.

Maximum three products. ... State every returned product with its amount before asking anything about payment; ask whether all can be paid today once ... Attempt counters belong to each product. A proposed common date is rolled and capped separately for each product. ... saved promises survive.

source.text: The opening and every sentence in this table are mandatory verbatim when the named situation occurs. ... The four forbidden pre-verification tokens are exactly `arrears`, `overdue`, `balance`, `payment`.

promise_write.confirm_phrase: May I save these arrangements together?

source.text: Promise failures: allow TWO EXTRA retries after the initial failure (three total attempts). A failed response means nothing committed. After three failures classify service failure and never claim success. (card: seek one explicit confirmation for the whole pending batch using "May I save these arrangements together?")

unresolved.text: Do not silently assume missing date components: ask for them. (No dedicated IR value for 'ask'; left at default.)

FINAL signed release instruction — effective 14 October. Its overrides (security order, 5 wrong answers, callbacks, 1–14 deadline, 2 retries, human ask-once) are applied in this policy; the documents do not say which values apply to calls before 14 October.

"Full-first still applies even to a later floor slot." The second 1–14 slot is described as 'floor by deadline'; the documents do not say exactly how full-first is applied in that slot when full has not yet been refused (IR attempt amount set to floor as the table states).

Be brief with third parties; never accept their security answers or payment promises. Ask whether the named holder is available before seeking a callback. No dedicated IR field; enforced by the template's third-party flow.
